questions.prompt: During a publicly visible security incident, who should normally communicate with the news media?
choices: Whichever analyst is working the incident
Any employee who happens to be contacted by a reporter
Designated public relations or communications staff
questions.explanation: Using designated spokespeople keeps messaging accurate and consistent and prevents disclosure of sensitive response details.

questions.prompt: Which incident response team member is MOST responsible for advising on breach notification requirements?
questions.explanation: Legal counsel interprets laws and contracts that determine whether, when, and how affected parties and regulators must be notified.

questions.prompt: In a business continuity plan, a call tree is used to:
choices: Route network traffic to the alternate site
Track the rotation order of backup tapes
Notify staff in a set order during an emergency
Rank recovery vendors by their pricing
questions.explanation: A call tree spreads notification responsibility so that every team member is contacted quickly and reliably when the plan is activated.

questions.prompt: When should a business continuity plan be updated?
choices: After major changes and at regular review intervals
Never, once senior management has formally approved it
Only after a real disaster has occurred
Only when an external auditor requests it
questions.explanation: An outdated plan may reference missing systems or departed staff, so it must be maintained as the organization changes and reviewed periodically.

questions.prompt: The average time it takes to repair a failed component and return it to service is known as:
questions.explanation: MTTR measures repair speed, while MTBF measures how long a component typically runs before it fails.

questions.prompt: A web server log shows an external host running a vulnerability scanner against it, but no attack has succeeded yet. In NIST terms, this is BEST described as a(n):
questions.explanation: A precursor signals that an incident may occur in the future. An indicator suggests an incident may have occurred or is occurring now.

questions.prompt: What is a major security weakness of discretionary access control (DAC)?
choices: Only a central administrator can change any permission
It requires every object to carry a security label
It cannot be used on common operating systems
Users may grant access too widely to others
questions.explanation: In DAC the owner decides who gets access, so users may share data too widely, and malware running as the user inherits that power.

questions.prompt: In a role-based access control system, an employee transfers from Sales to Finance. What is the BEST practice?
choices: Create a custom account that copies both roles
Remove the Sales role and assign the Finance role
Add the Finance role and keep the Sales role
Leave the roles unchanged until the annual review
questions.explanation: Removing the old role when assigning the new one prevents privilege creep and keeps access aligned with least privilege.

questions.prompt: A firewall allows or denies traffic based on a set of predefined rules that apply equally to all users. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Rule-based access control applies global rules, such as firewall rules, regardless of who the user is.

questions.prompt: In a mandatory access control system, which conditions must typically be met for a user to read a classified document?
choices: Ownership of the document and a strong password
Approval from any coworker with the same clearance
Clearance at or above the label plus need to know
questions.explanation: MAC compares the subject's clearance with the object's label, and need to know further restricts access even when clearance is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Which fence height is generally considered sufficient to deter a determined intruder?
choices: Any height, as long as it is painted
8 feet with strands of barbed wire on top
questions.explanation: Fences of 3 to 4 feet deter casual trespassers, 6 to 7 feet are hard to climb, and 8 feet topped with barbed wire deters determined intruders.

questions.prompt: What is a key weakness of a physical access system that relies only on badges?
choices: Badges always require a matching biometric scan
Badges cannot be deactivated once they are issued
Badges cannot record the time of each entry
A lost or stolen badge works for anyone holding it
questions.explanation: A badge is a single possession factor; adding a PIN or biometric ensures the person presenting it is the authorized holder.

questions.prompt: Bright lighting installed around a building's perimeter primarily serves which purposes?
choices: Deterring intruders and aiding their detection
Preventing all unauthorized entry on its own
questions.explanation: Lighting discourages intruders who fear being seen and improves the effectiveness of guards and CCTV, but it does not physically stop entry.

questions.prompt: In a shared colocation data center, which control BEST protects an organization's individual servers from other tenants?
choices: A warning sign posted on the main entrance
A visitor log kept at the lobby front desk
Locked cages or racks for the organization only
A shared door code issued to all tenants
questions.explanation: Locked cages and racks add a dedicated physical barrier around the organization's equipment inside the shared facility.

questions.prompt: A walkthrough finds passwords written on sticky notes attached to monitors. Which control would MOST directly address this?
choices: A clean desk policy with awareness training
Increasing the logging level on the perimeter firewall
questions.explanation: A clean desk policy requires sensitive information to be secured when unattended, and training explains why passwords must not be posted.

questions.prompt: Configuring workstations to lock automatically after a few minutes of inactivity mainly protects against:
choices: Someone using an unattended, logged-in session
questions.explanation: An automatic screen lock forces re-authentication, so a passerby cannot use an unattended session.

questions.prompt: A help desk technician needs to reset user passwords but should not be able to change security policies. Which approach follows least privilege?
choices: Share an administrator password with the technician
Add the technician to the Domain Admins group
Delegate only the password reset permission to the technician
Grant full control over the entire directory for convenience
questions.explanation: Delegating only the specific permission required gives the technician exactly the access the job needs and nothing more.

questions.prompt: Granting administrative rights only when needed and automatically revoking them after a short time is known as:
questions.explanation: Just-in-time access reduces standing privileges, shrinking the window in which elevated rights could be misused or stolen.

questions.prompt: A developer can write code and push it straight to production without any review or approval. Which principle is being violated?
questions.explanation: Separating development from deployment approval ensures no single person can introduce unauthorized or harmful changes alone.

questions.prompt: Segregation of duties can be defeated MOST directly by:
choices: Collusion between two or more employees
questions.explanation: Segregation of duties assumes people act independently; if they cooperate to commit fraud, the control can be bypassed. Job rotation and audits help detect this.

questions.prompt: Which approach BEST applies least privilege to a service account used by a backup application?
choices: Use the same account for all company services
Grant only the rights it needs and block interactive logon
Make it a member of every administrative group
Give it a password that never changes and share it widely
questions.explanation: Limiting a service account to its required rights and preventing interactive use reduces damage if it is compromised.

questions.prompt: A newly purchased network appliance ships with the username 'admin' and password 'admin'. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Change the default credentials before deployment
Keep the defaults so the vendor can support it
Write the credentials on the device's label
Disable logging to improve its performance
questions.explanation: Default credentials are publicly documented, and attackers routinely try them, so they must be changed immediately.

questions.prompt: Which attack tries a single common password against many different accounts to avoid triggering account lockouts?
questions.explanation: Password spraying spreads a few guesses across many accounts so no single account exceeds the lockout threshold.

questions.prompt: Attackers take username and password pairs leaked from one website's breach and try them on a bank's login page. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: Credential stuffing exploits password reuse by testing previously breached credential pairs against other services.

questions.prompt: Which control is MOST effective at stopping credential stuffing attacks from succeeding?
questions.explanation: Even if the stolen password is correct, the attacker still lacks the second factor, so MFA blocks most credential stuffing.

questions.prompt: An attacker tries every word from a large word list as the password for one account. This is a(n):
questions.explanation: A dictionary attack tests a list of likely words and common passwords, which is why strong, unpredictable passwords resist it.

questions.prompt: The point at which a biometric system's false acceptance rate equals its false rejection rate is the:
questions.explanation: The CER, also called the equal error rate, is used to compare biometric systems; a lower CER indicates a more accurate system.

questions.prompt: Employees of a partner company log in to your web portal using credentials issued by their own organization. This capability is called:
questions.explanation: Federation establishes trust between organizations so that one identity provider's authentication is accepted by another's services.

questions.prompt: Which standard uses XML-based assertions to exchange authentication information between an identity provider and a service provider for web single sign-on?
questions.explanation: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) passes signed assertions so users can sign on once and access multiple web applications.

questions.prompt: OAuth 2.0 is BEST described as:
choices: A standard for biometric authentication devices
An encryption algorithm for securing stored files
A framework for granting delegated authorization
A protocol for synchronizing system clocks
questions.explanation: OAuth lets a user authorize an application to access resources on their behalf without sharing their password.

questions.prompt: Which authentication protocol relies on a key distribution center that issues time-limited tickets?
questions.explanation: Kerberos uses tickets from a key distribution center so users authenticate once and then access services without resending passwords.

questions.prompt: Which AAA protocol encrypts the entire packet body and separates authentication, authorization, and accounting functions?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ encrypts the whole payload and handles the three AAA functions separately. RADIUS encrypts only the password and combines authentication with authorization.

questions.prompt: A pre-approved emergency administrator account that is used only when normal privileged access fails is commonly called a:
questions.explanation: Break-glass accounts are tightly protected and heavily monitored, and their use should trigger alerts and a review.

questions.prompt: Visitor badges should be:
choices: Kept by visitors for use on future visits
Distinct, time-limited, and collected on exit
Issued without recording the visitor's name
Identical to employee badges for simplicity
questions.explanation: Distinct, expiring visitor badges let staff spot visitors easily and prevent badges from being reused later.

questions.prompt: During a weekend, a sensor reports that a data center door was opened without a valid badge swipe. Which type of control generated this alert?
questions.explanation: A door contact alarm detects unauthorized physical entry after it happens, making it a physical detective control.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders physical security layers from the outermost to the innermost?
choices: Perimeter fence, building entrance, server room door, locked rack
Locked rack, server room door, building entrance, perimeter fence
Server room door, perimeter fence, locked rack, building entrance
Building entrance, perimeter fence, locked rack, server room door
questions.explanation: Layered physical security places successive barriers from the site boundary inward, so an intruder must defeat several controls to reach assets.

questions.prompt: Which role implements and maintains controls such as backups and access settings on behalf of the data owner?
questions.explanation: The owner decides how data should be protected, and the custodian, often IT staff, carries out those protections day to day.

questions.prompt: Why are FIDO2 security keys and passkeys considered resistant to phishing?
choices: The credential is bound to the real site's domain
They send the user's password by SMS
They use passwords longer than usual
They let users safely share one credential with coworkers
questions.explanation: FIDO2 uses public key cryptography tied to the site's origin, so a look-alike phishing site cannot obtain a usable credential.

questions.prompt: An attacker logged in as a standard user exploits a software flaw to gain administrator rights. This is known as:
questions.explanation: Privilege escalation is gaining higher rights than authorized. Privilege creep is the gradual buildup of legitimate access over time.

questions.prompt: An audit finds active accounts belonging to employees who left the company months ago. These are called:
questions.explanation: Orphaned accounts lack an active owner and are attractive to attackers; timely deprovisioning prevents them.

questions.prompt: An access review reveals that a user has permissions that do not match their current job. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Validate with the data owner, then remove the excess access
Ignore it until the next annual access review
Grant the same access to the whole team for consistency
questions.explanation: The reviewer should validate the finding with the accountable owner and then revoke unnecessary access to restore least privilege.

questions.prompt: Which physical control is a preventive measure against theft of a laptop left on a desk in an open office?
choices: A sign stating that theft will be prosecuted
A CCTV camera recording the office
An inventory audit at the end of the year
A cable lock attaching it to the desk
questions.explanation: A cable lock physically prevents easy removal. The camera is detective, the sign is deterrent, and the audit detects loss afterward.

questions.prompt: Administrators must log in to servers remotely over the internet. Which control is MOST important to require?
questions.explanation: Remote privileged access is a prime target, and MFA ensures a stolen password alone is not enough to gain access.

questions.prompt: What is a drawback of setting a very low account lockout threshold?
choices: It prevents logging of failed attempts
It makes user passwords much easier for attackers to guess
Attackers can trigger lockouts to deny service
questions.explanation: Lockouts can be abused for denial of service, so thresholds and lockout durations must balance security against availability.

questions.prompt: Where is the BEST location for a server room within a building?
choices: The ground floor beside the main lobby
An interior room away from exterior walls
A top-floor room with large windows
A basement below the local water line
questions.explanation: An interior location reduces exposure to break-ins, weather, and flooding while making access easier to control.

questions.prompt: A user must enter a password and then approve a push notification on a registered phone. Which principle does adding the second step BEST support?
questions.explanation: Adding an independent factor layers protection, so compromising the password alone does not grant access.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a logical control that enforces least privilege on a shared network folder?
choices: A signed acceptable use policy for staff
File share permissions limited to those who need them
A locked door on the room that houses the file server
Security guards stationed in the lobby
questions.explanation: File and share permissions are technical (logical) controls that restrict what each user can do with the data.

questions.prompt: A company requires that new accounts be created only after a manager submits an approved request. This process MAINLY ensures that:
choices: Accounts never need to be reviewed again
Access is authorized and documented first
Passwords are encrypted while in transit
Users can choose their own permissions
questions.explanation: Approval-based provisioning ties every account to a legitimate business need and creates an audit trail.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes a difference between authentication and authorization?
choices: Authentication proves identity; authorization grants rights
Authorization verifies a user's identity using a password
Authentication and authorization mean the same thing
questions.explanation: A system first authenticates the subject's identity and then authorizes specific actions based on permissions.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer is responsible for data formatting, character encoding, compression, and encryption?
questions.explanation: Layer 6, the presentation layer, translates data into a format the application layer can use and handles encoding, compression, and encryption.

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer establishes, manages, and terminates communication sessions between applications?
questions.explanation: Layer 5, the session layer, controls dialogs between applications, including setting up and tearing down sessions.

questions.prompt: A network hub, which simply repeats electrical signals out of every port, operates at which OSI layer?
questions.explanation: Hubs work only with raw signals and have no awareness of MAC or IP addresses, placing them at the physical layer.

questions.prompt: At the transport layer, a unit of TCP data is called a:
questions.explanation: TCP data at Layer 4 is a segment; Layer 3 uses packets, Layer 2 uses frames, and Layer 1 transmits bits.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly shows how data is encapsulated as it moves down the OSI layers on the sending host?
questions.explanation: Each lower layer adds its own header: the transport layer creates segments, the network layer creates packets, and the data link layer creates frames that are sent as bits.

questions.prompt: Which default port does LDAP over TLS (LDAPS) use?
questions.explanation: LDAPS uses TCP 636. Plain LDAP uses 389.

questions.prompt: SNMP agents listen for management queries on which default UDP port?
questions.explanation: SNMP queries go to UDP 161 on the agent, while SNMP traps are sent to UDP 162 on the manager.

questions.prompt: Modern Windows file sharing using SMB runs directly over which TCP port?
questions.explanation: SMB runs directly over TCP 445 on modern systems; 139 was used for SMB over NetBIOS. Port 445 should never be exposed to the internet.

questions.prompt: Network Time Protocol (NTP), used to synchronize clocks, uses which port?
questions.explanation: NTP uses UDP 123. Accurate time matters for log correlation and for protocols such as Kerberos.

questions.prompt: Which port is used by IMAP over SSL/TLS for secure email retrieval?
questions.explanation: IMAPS uses 993. Plain IMAP uses 143, and POP3S uses 995.

questions.prompt: FTP uses which port for its control channel, where commands and credentials are sent?
questions.explanation: FTP sends commands over TCP 21 and uses TCP 20 for data in active mode. Credentials cross port 21 in cleartext.

questions.prompt: Syslog messages are traditionally sent to a log server on which port?
questions.explanation: Traditional syslog uses UDP 514; secure syslog over TLS commonly uses TCP 6514.

questions.prompt: SFTP, which transfers files securely, runs over which default port?
questions.explanation: SFTP is a subsystem of SSH and uses TCP 22. FTPS, a different protocol, commonly uses 990 for implicit TLS.

questions.prompt: Which protocol maps an IPv4 address to a device's MAC address on a local network?
questions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) finds the hardware address for a known IP address on the local segment.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends forged ARP replies so that hosts send traffic meant for the default gateway to the attacker's machine. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: ARP poisoning corrupts hosts' ARP caches, letting the attacker intercept or modify traffic as an on-path attacker.

questions.prompt: Users who type their bank's correct URL are sent to a fake site because their DNS resolver has stored forged records. This is:
choices: ARP spoofing on the local segment
questions.explanation: DNS cache poisoning inserts false records into a resolver so legitimate names resolve to attacker-controlled addresses.

questions.prompt: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
questions.explanation: In IPv6, ::1 is the loopback address, which is equivalent to 127.0.0.1 in IPv4.

questions.prompt: How is an IPv6 address written?
choices: As four decimal numbers separated by periods
As eight groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons
As six pairs of hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128 bits written as eight 16-bit hexadecimal groups, which can be shortened with the :: notation.

questions.prompt: A workstation reports an IP address of 169.254.10.20. What does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: The host is using a public internet address
The host could not reach a DHCP server
The host is configured as the default gateway
The host has been assigned an IPv6 address
questions.explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the APIPA (link-local) range that Windows assigns itself when DHCP is unreachable.

questions.prompt: A subnet written as /24 in CIDR notation has which subnet mask?
questions.explanation: A /24 means 24 network bits, which is 255.255.255.0 and leaves 8 bits for hosts.

questions.prompt: WPA3-Personal replaces the WPA2 pre-shared key handshake with which method to resist offline password guessing?
questions.explanation: SAE, a form of the Dragonfly handshake, prevents attackers from capturing a handshake and cracking the passphrase offline.

questions.prompt: A company wants each employee to join the corporate Wi-Fi with their own directory credentials rather than a shared password. What is the BEST choice?
choices: WPA3-Enterprise using 802.1X and a RADIUS server
WPA3-Personal with one shared passphrase for all staff
An open network with a hidden SSID
questions.explanation: Enterprise mode authenticates each user individually through 802.1X, allowing per-user access control and revocation.

questions.prompt: Disabling the broadcast of a wireless network's SSID is considered a weak security measure because:
choices: The name can still be found by sniffing traffic
It encrypts traffic with an outdated algorithm
It blocks legitimate users from connecting
It forces all wireless clients to use WEP
questions.explanation: Hidden SSIDs still appear in probe requests and other frames, so they provide obscurity rather than real protection.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets and never completes the handshake, exhausting the server's connection table. This is a:
questions.explanation: A SYN flood leaves many half-open connections, consuming server resources and causing a denial of service.

questions.prompt: A network of malware-infected computers controlled remotely by an attacker through command-and-control servers is called a:
questions.explanation: Botnets are commonly used to launch DDoS attacks, send spam, and spread malware on the attacker's command.

questions.prompt: A vulnerability that is unknown to the vendor and has no patch available when it is exploited is called a:
questions.explanation: Zero-day exploits target flaws before a fix exists, so signature-based defenses often fail to detect them.

questions.prompt: An attacker enters ' OR 1=1 -- into the username field of a login form to bypass authentication. This is:
questions.explanation: SQL injection inserts SQL syntax into input that is passed to a database query. Parameterized queries and input validation prevent it.

questions.prompt: An attacker posts a comment containing JavaScript that runs in the browsers of other users who view the page. This is:
questions.explanation: XSS injects malicious scripts into content served to other users, which can steal session cookies or perform actions on their behalf.

questions.prompt: Sending more input than a program's memory area can hold, overwriting adjacent memory to run malicious code, is a:
questions.explanation: Buffer overflows exploit missing bounds checks; input validation and memory protections such as ASLR help prevent them.

questions.prompt: An attacker captures a valid authentication exchange on the network and later resends it to gain access. This is a(n):
questions.explanation: Replay attacks reuse captured credentials or tokens; timestamps, nonces, and session tokens defend against them.

questions.prompt: An IPS is typically deployed in which way so that it can block malicious traffic?
choices: Inline, so traffic passes through it
On a mirror port that only copies traffic
Outside the network with no connection to it
questions.explanation: Because an IPS must stop traffic in real time, it sits inline. An IDS commonly monitors a copy of traffic from a span or mirror port.

questions.prompt: An IDS fails to generate an alert during a real attack. This outcome is called a:
questions.explanation: A false negative misses actual malicious activity, which is dangerous because the attack goes unnoticed.

questions.prompt: Compared with a traditional stateful firewall, a next-generation firewall (NGFW) adds:
choices: Application awareness and deep packet inspection
Physical protection for the server room
Only the ability to filter traffic by port number
questions.explanation: NGFWs identify applications and users, inspect payloads, and often integrate intrusion prevention.

questions.prompt: How does a typical firewall process its rule list when a packet arrives?
choices: From top to bottom, applying the first rule that matches
By applying every matching rule at the same time
From bottom to top, applying the last match
Randomly, to prevent attackers from predicting it
questions.explanation: Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins, so rule placement matters and specific rules belong above general ones.

questions.prompt: Employees often connect their laptops to public Wi-Fi in hotels. Which control BEST protects each laptop from other devices on those networks?
choices: A VLAN on the office switch
A DMZ for the company web server
A perimeter firewall installed at corporate headquarters
A host-based firewall enabled on each laptop
questions.explanation: A host-based firewall travels with the device and filters traffic even when the device is outside the corporate network.

questions.prompt: A server that makes web requests on behalf of internal clients and can filter or log the sites they visit is a:
questions.explanation: A forward proxy sits between users and the internet, enabling content filtering, caching, and monitoring of outbound web traffic.

questions.prompt: A deliberately vulnerable decoy system set up to attract attackers and study their methods is called a:
questions.explanation: Honeypots divert attackers from real assets and reveal their techniques; any interaction with one is suspicious by definition.

questions.prompt: A remote user's VPN sends only corporate-bound traffic through the tunnel while other internet traffic goes directly to the internet. This configuration is called:
questions.explanation: Split tunneling saves bandwidth, but corporate security controls cannot inspect the user's direct internet traffic.

questions.prompt: Which IPsec mode encrypts the entire original IP packet, including its header, and is typically used for site-to-site VPNs?
questions.explanation: Tunnel mode wraps the whole original packet inside a new one. Transport mode protects only the payload.

questions.prompt: Which IPsec protocol provides confidentiality by encrypting the payload?
questions.explanation: ESP provides encryption plus integrity. AH provides integrity and authentication only, with no encryption.

questions.prompt: Which IEEE standard provides port-based network access control, requiring devices to authenticate before a switch port allows traffic?
questions.explanation: 802.1X uses a supplicant, authenticator, and authentication server, usually RADIUS. 802.1Q defines VLAN tagging.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic lets resources automatically scale up during peak demand and back down afterward?
questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity allows capacity to expand and contract quickly with demand, so customers pay only for what they use.

questions.prompt: Several hospitals share a cloud infrastructure built to meet their common regulatory requirements. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A community cloud is shared by organizations with common concerns, such as compliance needs, and is not open to the general public.

questions.prompt: A company outsources the monitoring and management of its firewalls and security alerts to a third party. This provider is BEST described as a(n):
questions.explanation: An MSSP delivers security operations such as monitoring and device management as a service; contracts and SLAs define its responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Why should IoT devices such as smart cameras usually be placed on a separate network segment?
choices: They cannot obtain IP addresses on normal networks
They require much faster network connections than workstations
They often lack updates, so isolation limits any compromise
Separating them makes the devices cheaper to buy
questions.explanation: Segmenting IoT devices prevents an attacker who compromises one from easily reaching critical internal systems.

questions.prompt: Why is a network switch considered more secure than a hub?
choices: It sends frames only to the destination's port
It assigns IP addresses to every device
It blocks all malware at the application layer
questions.explanation: A hub sends every frame to all ports, making sniffing easy, while a switch uses MAC address tables to deliver frames only where they belong.

questions.prompt: A control system network is physically disconnected from all other networks, including the internet. This is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An air gap provides strong isolation, although removable media and insiders can still bridge it.

questions.prompt: Which extension adds digital signatures to DNS responses so that resolvers can verify they have not been forged?
questions.explanation: DNSSEC lets resolvers validate the origin and integrity of DNS data, defending against cache poisoning. It does not encrypt queries.

questions.prompt: Which hashing algorithm is considered broken because practical collisions can be produced, and should not be used for security purposes?
questions.explanation: Researchers can generate MD5 collisions easily, so it is unsuitable for signatures or integrity checks. The SHA-2 family remains secure.

questions.prompt: When two different inputs produce the same hash value, this is called a:
questions.explanation: A secure hash function makes collisions computationally infeasible to find; once practical collisions exist, the algorithm is considered broken.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an asymmetric encryption algorithm?
questions.explanation: RSA uses a public and private key pair. AES, 3DES, and Blowfish are symmetric algorithms that use one shared key.

questions.prompt: Ten users each need to communicate privately with every other user using symmetric encryption. How many unique keys are required?
questions.explanation: Each pair of users needs its own shared secret key, so n(n-1)/2 keys are required: 10 x 9 / 2 = 45. This scaling problem is one reason asymmetric cryptography is used for key exchange.

questions.prompt: A company enables BitLocker full-disk encryption on all laptops. Which data state does this PRIMARILY protect?
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption protects stored data if a device is lost or stolen. TLS protects data in transit.

questions.prompt: Which entity issues and digitally signs certificates within a public key infrastructure?
questions.explanation: A CA vouches for the binding between an identity and a public key by signing the certificate with its own private key.

questions.prompt: To verify a digital signature on a message from Alice, Bob should use:
questions.explanation: Alice signs with her private key, and anyone can verify the signature with her public key, confirming authenticity and integrity.

questions.prompt: Which AES key lengths are defined by the standard?
questions.explanation: AES supports 128-, 192-, and 256-bit keys. 56 bits is the DES key size, and 2048 bits is a common RSA key size.

questions.prompt: A company press release has already been published on its public website. Which classification level is MOST appropriate for it?
questions.explanation: Information intentionally released to the public requires no confidentiality protection, so it is classified as public.

questions.prompt: Which method is MOST appropriate for disposing of printed documents containing confidential customer data?
choices: Placing them in an office recycling bin
questions.explanation: Cross-cut shredding reduces paper to small pieces that are very hard to reassemble; recycling or tearing leaves the data readable.

questions.prompt: Under NIST SP 800-88, overwriting media so that data cannot be recovered with standard tools, while allowing the media to be reused, is called:
questions.explanation: NIST defines three levels: clear, purge, and destroy. Clearing protects against simple, non-invasive recovery and keeps the media usable.

questions.prompt: Which sanitization method is well suited to quickly rendering data on a self-encrypting SSD unrecoverable while keeping the drive reusable?
questions.explanation: Cryptographic erase destroys the encryption key, making the data unreadable. Degaussing does not work on flash storage, and a quick format leaves data recoverable.

questions.prompt: Which event is MOST important to capture in security logs?
questions.explanation: Failed privileged logins can indicate brute-force or credential attacks and are key evidence for detection and investigation.

questions.prompt: Which measure BEST protects logs from being altered by an attacker who gains administrator access to a server?
choices: Keeping logs only on the local server's disk
Allowing all users to edit the log files
Turning off logging during maintenance windows
Forwarding logs in real time to immutable storage
questions.explanation: Immutable, off-host storage preserves log integrity because the attacker cannot change records once they are written.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to establish a baseline of normal network and system activity?
choices: It makes unusual activity easier to recognize
It guarantees that no attacks will succeed
It removes the need to collect logs
It replaces the need for patching
questions.explanation: Monitoring tools and analysts compare current behavior against the baseline to spot anomalies that may signal an attack.

questions.prompt: Which type of tool automates incident response workflows by running playbooks across security products?
questions.explanation: Security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platforms automate repetitive response steps and coordinate tools.

questions.prompt: Monitoring outbound (egress) network traffic is MOST useful for detecting:
choices: Power outages affecting the data center
Users who frequently forget their account passwords
questions.explanation: Egress monitoring reveals unusual outbound transfers and connections that indicate stolen data or compromised hosts.

questions.prompt: A tool detects an employee trying to email a spreadsheet of credit card numbers to a personal address and blocks the message. This tool is:
questions.explanation: DLP inspects content for sensitive data patterns and blocks or alerts on unauthorized transfers.

questions.prompt: Which resource provides consensus-based, freely available secure configuration guides for operating systems and applications?
questions.explanation: The Center for Internet Security publishes benchmarks that organizations commonly use as the basis for hardening baselines.

questions.prompt: After deploying a security patch to production servers, what should the team do next?
choices: Disable logging on the patched servers
Verify it installed and systems work correctly
Delete the associated change request record
Remove the systems from the asset inventory
questions.explanation: Verification confirms that the vulnerability is closed and that the patch did not break functionality, and it completes the change record.

questions.prompt: Over time, servers gradually deviate from their approved secure configuration because of undocumented changes. This is called:
questions.explanation: Configuration drift weakens security; regular scans against the baseline and enforced change management help detect and correct it.

questions.prompt: Why is an accurate asset inventory the foundation of configuration management?
choices: It replaces the need for regular backups
It eliminates the need for network firewalls
It encrypts all listed devices automatically
You cannot secure systems you do not know exist
questions.explanation: Unknown, unmanaged devices are left unpatched and unmonitored, so a complete inventory is required before baselines can be applied.

questions.prompt: Which tool continuously monitors endpoints for suspicious behavior and lets analysts investigate and contain threats remotely?
choices: Wireless access point with built-in controller
questions.explanation: EDR goes beyond signature-based antivirus by recording endpoint activity, detecting malicious behavior, and supporting remote response actions.

questions.prompt: Which policy tells customers and users how an organization collects, uses, shares, and protects their personal information?
questions.explanation: A privacy policy documents personal data practices and is often required by privacy laws such as the GDPR.

questions.prompt: When should employees typically acknowledge the acceptable use policy?
choices: Only when they leave the company
At onboarding and periodically, such as yearly
Only after they have violated it
Never, because it applies only to IT staff
questions.explanation: Signed acknowledgment at hire and on a recurring basis ensures staff know the rules and supports enforcement.

questions.prompt: In change management, which group typically reviews, prioritizes, and approves proposed changes?
questions.explanation: The CAB evaluates the risk, impact, and readiness of changes before they are approved for implementation.

questions.prompt: A critical production outage requires an immediate configuration fix outside the normal change schedule. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Make the change without any record to save time
Use the emergency change process, then document and review
Wait for the next scheduled monthly change board meeting
Ask affected users to apply the fix themselves
questions.explanation: Emergency change procedures allow fast action while preserving accountability through documentation and after-the-fact review.

questions.prompt: Which method is MOST effective for measuring whether security awareness training is changing employee behavior?
choices: Recording the time of day training was taken
Asking employees whether they enjoyed the training
Counting the number of slides in the course
questions.explanation: Simulated phishing shows how many users click or report suspicious messages, giving measurable evidence of behavior change.

questions.prompt: A phishing email crafted specifically for a company's chief financial officer is an example of:
questions.explanation: Whaling is spear phishing aimed at senior executives, who have high authority and access.

questions.prompt: An attacker researches a specific employee on social media and sends a tailored email mentioning their manager and current project. This is:
questions.explanation: Spear phishing uses personal details to target a specific individual, making the message far more convincing than generic phishing.

questions.prompt: Attackers leave infected USB drives labeled 'Salary Review' in a company parking lot, hoping employees will plug them in. This technique is called:
questions.explanation: Baiting uses curiosity or greed to lure victims into using malicious media or downloads.

questions.prompt: An employee receives an email that looks suspicious and asks them to log in through a link. What is the BEST action?
choices: Reply to the sender to ask if it is legitimate
Report it to security without clicking the link
Forward it to all coworkers as a warning
Click the link to check whether it is real
questions.explanation: Reporting lets security analyze and block the threat, while clicking, forwarding, or replying can spread or confirm the attack.

questions.prompt: A caller claims to be a senior executive and demands that an employee bypass procedures immediately. Which social engineering principles are being exploited?
questions.explanation: Attackers impersonate powerful figures and create time pressure so victims comply without verifying the request.

questions.prompt: A company expects to be sued and must preserve relevant email even though its retention schedule says to delete it. This requirement is called a:
questions.explanation: A legal hold suspends normal deletion for data relevant to anticipated or ongoing litigation, overriding the retention schedule.

questions.prompt: A payment system replaces credit card numbers with random substitute values and stores the real numbers in a separate secure vault. This technique is:
questions.explanation: Tokenization swaps sensitive data for meaningless tokens, reducing the systems that handle real card data. Masking only hides part of the value on display.

questions.prompt: A customer service screen shows only the last four digits of a customer's Social Security number. This technique is called:
questions.explanation: Masking obscures part of a value so staff see only what they need, reducing exposure of sensitive data.

questions.prompt: An organization implements an information security management system and seeks certification against ISO/IEC 27001. What is the MAIN benefit?
choices: Elimination of the need for internal risk assessments
Automatic compliance with every national privacy law
Independent assurance that its ISMS meets a recognized standard
Legal immunity from all data breach lawsuits
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001 certification shows an accredited auditor has verified the ISMS. It does not grant legal immunity or replace risk assessment, which the standard itself requires.

questions.prompt: What is a key security advantage of a biometric door reader over a badge-only reader?
choices: It never produces false rejections of valid users
It removes the need to log door entries
The credential cannot easily be lent or handed to someone else
It costs less to install than badge readers
questions.explanation: A fingerprint or palm print stays with the person, so unlike a badge it cannot simply be passed to another individual. Biometrics still have error rates and should still be logged.

questions.prompt: A retailer collected customers' addresses only to ship orders, then starts using them for a marketing campaign without telling customers. Which privacy principle is MOST directly violated?
questions.explanation: Purpose limitation means personal data is used only for the purposes it was collected for, unless the person agrees otherwise. Data minimization limits how much is collected.

questions.prompt: A research team permanently removes all identifiers from a dataset so that individuals can never be re-identified, even by the team. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Anonymization irreversibly removes the link to individuals. Pseudonymization replaces identifiers with values that can be re-linked using separately held information.

questions.prompt: Before any safeguards are put in place, an analyst rates the risk of a public web server being defaced as high. What is this level of risk called?
questions.explanation: Inherent risk is the level of risk before controls are applied. Residual risk is what remains after controls.

questions.prompt: In quantitative risk analysis, what does the exposure factor (EF) represent?
choices: The number of times a threat occurs per year
The total yearly cost of all incidents
The dollar value of the asset
Percentage of asset value lost per incident
questions.explanation: EF is the portion of asset value lost in a single event. Asset value multiplied by EF gives the single loss expectancy.

questions.prompt: A piece of code is written specifically to take advantage of a known flaw in a web server to gain access. What is this code called?
questions.explanation: An exploit is the method or code that takes advantage of a vulnerability. The vulnerability is the weakness itself.

questions.prompt: Which U.S. law requires financial institutions to explain their information-sharing practices and protect customers' nonpublic personal financial information?
choices: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
questions.explanation: GLBA covers financial institutions and customer financial data. HIPAA covers health information, and SOX covers financial reporting controls.

questions.prompt: Which organization develops the 802 family of networking standards, including 802.11 Wi-Fi and 802.3 Ethernet?
questions.explanation: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers publishes the 802 standards. The IETF develops internet protocols through RFCs.

questions.prompt: Each entry in a company's risk register lists the person responsible for monitoring that risk and making sure its treatment is carried out. What is this person called?
questions.explanation: A risk owner is accountable for managing a specific risk and its treatment plan. A data custodian implements controls on data.

questions.prompt: An employee accidentally emails a spreadsheet of customers' Social Security numbers to the wrong outside recipient. Which part of the CIA triad is MOST affected?
questions.explanation: Sensitive data was disclosed to an unauthorized party, which is a loss of confidentiality. The data itself was not altered or made unavailable.

questions.prompt: What is the PRIMARY purpose of an organization's information security program?
choices: To make every system impossible to attack
To support business goals by managing risk
To replace the need for management oversight
questions.explanation: Security exists to support the organization's mission by managing risk to an acceptable level. Eliminating all risk is not achievable or cost-effective.

questions.prompt: An employee with no malicious intent clicks a phishing link and lets an attacker into the network. How is this employee BEST categorized?
questions.explanation: Insiders can cause harm through carelessness or mistakes as well as malice. Training and technical controls help reduce unintentional insider risk.

questions.prompt: An attacker with little technical skill downloads a ready-made attack tool and runs it against random websites. Which type of threat actor is this?
questions.explanation: Script kiddies rely on tools created by others and lack deep skills. Nation-state and APT actors are highly skilled and well resourced.

questions.prompt: A criminal group runs ransomware campaigns and sells stolen card numbers. What is its MOST likely motivation?
questions.explanation: Organized crime groups are primarily motivated by money. Hacktivists act for political or social causes, and nation-states often seek espionage.

questions.prompt: A firewall must allow clients to obtain IP addresses from a DHCP server. Which ports are used?
questions.explanation: DHCP servers listen on UDP 67 and clients use UDP 68. SNMP uses 161 and 162, and FTP uses 20 and 21.

questions.prompt: How many layers does the TCP/IP model, as commonly taught, contain?
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP model has four layers: network access (link), internet, transport and application. The OSI model has seven.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends packets with a forged source IP address so they appear to come from a trusted internal host. What is this called?
questions.explanation: IP spoofing falsifies the source address to impersonate another system or hide the attacker's identity.

questions.prompt: A startup rents computing resources from a provider whose infrastructure is shared and available to any paying customer. Which cloud deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A public cloud is offered to the general public over the internet. A private cloud serves a single organization.

questions.prompt: A company uses a web-based email service where the provider manages the application, servers and storage, and the company only manages users and data. Which cloud service model is this?
questions.explanation: In SaaS, the provider delivers a complete application. In IaaS and PaaS, the customer manages more of the stack.

questions.prompt: A company applies security policies to individual workloads so that even servers in the same subnet can communicate only as explicitly allowed. What is this approach called?
questions.explanation: Microsegmentation enforces fine-grained policies between individual workloads, limiting lateral movement inside the network.

questions.prompt: A data center needs fire suppression that will not cause water damage to servers. Which system is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Clean agent systems put out fires without leaving residue or water, protecting electronic equipment. Water and powder can damage hardware.

questions.prompt: Why must humidity in a data center be kept within a moderate range?
choices: Too dry causes static; too humid causes condensation
Humidity matters only for tape storage media
High humidity improves cooling, so it should be maximized
Too dry causes condensation; too humid causes static
questions.explanation: Air that is too dry encourages electrostatic discharge, while air that is too humid can lead to condensation and corrosion.

questions.prompt: A data center's UPS batteries last about 15 minutes. Which addition is needed to keep systems running during a power outage lasting several hours?
questions.explanation: A UPS bridges short gaps, while a generator supplies power for extended outages once it starts.

questions.prompt: In a data center, server racks are arranged so that equipment intakes face one aisle and exhausts face the next. What is the purpose of this layout?
choices: To reduce the number of power circuits needed per row
To shorten network cable runs between racks
To keep hot exhaust from mixing with intake air
To keep visitors physically away from servers
questions.explanation: Hot aisle/cold aisle layouts prevent hot exhaust from mixing with cool intake air, improving cooling efficiency.

questions.prompt: Which protocol does the ping utility use to test whether a host is reachable?
questions.explanation: Ping sends ICMP echo requests and waits for echo replies. ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses.

questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of IPv6 over IPv4?
choices: It no longer needs any security controls
It removes the need for routers
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, providing far more addresses than IPv4's 32-bit space and reducing the need for NAT.

questions.prompt: A server room door opens only when a person enters a programmable numeric code on a keypad. What type of lock is this?
questions.explanation: A cipher lock uses a programmable keypad code. The code can be changed when staff leave, unlike a key-based lock.

questions.prompt: Users keep changing their password and then immediately changing it back to the old one. Which setting prevents this?
choices: An account lockout after three failed attempts
Password history plus a minimum password age
questions.explanation: Password history blocks reuse of recent passwords, and a minimum age stops users from cycling through changes quickly to get the old one back.

questions.prompt: A system identifies users by the unique rhythm and timing of how they type. Which type of biometric is this?
questions.explanation: Keystroke dynamics measure behavior. Physiological biometrics, such as fingerprints or iris patterns, measure physical traits.

questions.prompt: A security team builds a table that lists every user down one side, every resource across the top, and the permissions in each cell. What is this called?
questions.explanation: An access control matrix maps subjects to objects with their permissions. Each column corresponds to an object's access control list.

questions.prompt: A contractor is hired for a three-month project. Which account setting BEST makes sure their access does not outlast the engagement?
questions.explanation: Setting an expiration date ensures the account is disabled automatically if offboarding is missed.

questions.prompt: A company designs its campus with clear sight lines, good lighting and landscaping that naturally guides visitors to a single main entrance. Which approach is this?
choices: Defense in depth through network segmentation
questions.explanation: CPTED uses the physical environment, such as visibility, lighting and natural access control, to discourage crime.

questions.prompt: Equipment has gone missing from a server room. Which source BEST shows who entered the room and when?
questions.explanation: Electronic badge systems record each entry with the badge holder and a timestamp, supporting investigations.

questions.prompt: Emergency exit doors in a secure building must let people out freely during a fire. Which control BEST discourages employees from using them for normal entry and exit?
choices: An audible alarm on the door
A keypad code required to exit
Chaining the doors shut after hours
questions.explanation: Alarmed emergency exits allow safe egress while deterring routine misuse. Locking or chaining exits endangers life safety.

questions.prompt: Before a new employee can use a fingerprint reader, the system scans their finger several times to create a stored template. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Enrollment captures and stores the biometric template that later scans are compared against.

questions.prompt: An employee is terminated this morning. Besides disabling their network accounts, which physical access step should be taken right away?
choices: Change the Wi-Fi password next month
questions.explanation: Badges should be deactivated and retrieved at termination so the former employee cannot enter the facility.

questions.prompt: A master key that opens several office doors has been lost and cannot be found. What is the BEST response?
choices: Post a notice asking for its return
Issue the same key to more people
Rekey or replace the affected locks
questions.explanation: A lost master key means anyone who finds it can enter, so the locks must be rekeyed or replaced to restore control.

questions.prompt: After classifying a report as Confidential, an employee adds a header and footer stating 'Confidential' on every page. Which data handling step is this?
questions.explanation: Labeling marks data with its classification so people handle it correctly. Classification decides the level, and labeling communicates it.

questions.prompt: A website uses HTTPS so that login credentials cannot be read while traveling across the internet. Which data state is being protected?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (TLS) encrypts data as it moves across networks. Full-disk encryption protects data at rest.

questions.prompt: Under NIST SP 800-88, which sanitization level protects against even laboratory recovery techniques, using methods such as degaussing or secure erase commands?
questions.explanation: Purging defeats laboratory-level recovery attempts. Clearing protects only against simple, non-invasive recovery with standard tools.

questions.prompt: Old project records are no longer used day to day but must be kept for seven years for legal reasons. What should be done with them?
choices: Post them to the company intranet
Delete them now to free up storage space
Keep copies on every user's laptop
Move them to secure archival storage
questions.explanation: Archiving keeps inactive data protected and retrievable for the retention period, after which it is securely destroyed.

questions.prompt: Ten users each need a key pair to exchange encrypted messages using asymmetric cryptography. How many keys are required in total?
questions.explanation: Each user needs one public and one private key, so 10 x 2 = 20. The symmetric equivalent would need 45 shared keys.

questions.prompt: A spreadsheet of salaries is open and being edited in a computer's memory. Which data state is this?
questions.explanation: Data actively being processed in memory or by the CPU is in use. Stored files are at rest, and data on the network is in transit.

questions.prompt: An organization wants to reduce the risk of malware from unknown flash drives and data leaving on personal USB devices. Which policy addresses this?
questions.explanation: A removable media policy controls whether and how USB drives and similar devices can be used, often backed by technical controls.

questions.prompt: A caller offers an employee a free gift card in exchange for 'confirming' their network login details for a survey. Which social engineering technique is this?
questions.explanation: Quid pro quo offers something in return for information or access. Tailgating and shoulder surfing are physical techniques.

questions.prompt: An audit discovers a department using an unapproved cloud file-sharing app that IT does not know about or manage. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Shadow IT is technology used without IT's approval or oversight, which creates unmanaged security and compliance risk.

questions.prompt: Several security alerts arrive at once, and the response team assesses each one to decide which should be handled first based on severity and impact. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Triage prioritizes incidents so the most serious ones receive attention first. Eradication removes the cause after containment.

questions.prompt: An organization runs nightly backups but has never restored from them. What is the BEST way to confirm the backups can actually be used in a disaster?
questions.explanation: Only a test restore proves that backups are complete and recoverable. More frequent or encrypted backups do not confirm restorability.

questions.prompt: Team members individually review copies of the disaster recovery plan to confirm that contact lists and procedures are accurate, without meeting or touching any systems. Which test is this?
questions.explanation: A checklist test is the least disruptive DR test, in which participants review the plan for accuracy and completeness.

questions.prompt: Antivirus software alerts that malware was detected on a workstation right now. In incident response terms, what is this alert?
questions.explanation: An indicator is a sign that an incident may have occurred or is occurring. A precursor suggests an incident may happen in the future.

questions.prompt: An organization wants the fastest, simplest restore process after a failure and is willing to use more storage space. Which backup approach should it favor?
questions.explanation: A full backup restores from a single set, so recovery is fastest. Incremental backups save space but need the full backup plus every incremental.

questions.prompt: A recipient wants assurance that a software update is genuine and really came from the claimed vendor rather than an imposter. Which security property is this?
questions.explanation: Authenticity is assurance that data or a message is genuine and comes from its claimed source. Digital signatures are a common way to provide it.

questions.prompt: According to the preamble of the ISC2 Code of Ethics, strict adherence to the Code is:
choices: Required only while employed in security
questions.explanation: The preamble states that strict adherence to the Code is a condition of certification. Members can lose their certification for violations.

questions.prompt: A development team builds privacy protections, such as collecting minimal data and encrypting it by default, into a new app from the first design stage rather than adding them later. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Privacy by design means building privacy into systems from the start and by default. Purpose limitation restricts how collected data may be used.

questions.prompt: In risk management, the probability that a particular threat will exploit a given vulnerability is known as:
questions.explanation: Likelihood is the chance that a threat will exploit a vulnerability. Impact is the magnitude of harm if it does.

questions.prompt: In risk management, the magnitude of harm an organization would suffer if a threat successfully exploited a vulnerability is called the:
questions.explanation: Impact measures how much damage results from a realized threat. Combined with likelihood, it determines the level of risk.

questions.prompt: Which U.S. law protects the privacy of student education records held by schools that receive federal funding?
questions.explanation: FERPA protects the privacy of student education records. HIPAA covers health information, GLBA financial institutions and SOX financial reporting.

questions.prompt: A gaming website aimed at young children must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting personal information from users under 13. Which U.S. law requires this?
questions.explanation: The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) governs online collection of personal information from children under 13 in the United States.

questions.prompt: Which NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 function covers restoring assets and operations that were affected by a cybersecurity incident?
questions.explanation: The Recover function focuses on restoring assets and operations after an incident. Respond covers actions taken to address a detected incident.

questions.prompt: An organization starts its NIST Cybersecurity Framework program by building an inventory of its hardware, software and data, and understanding its current risks. Which CSF function does this activity belong to?
questions.explanation: Asset management and risk assessment are part of the Identify function, which helps an organization understand what it needs to protect.

questions.prompt: An organization certified under ISO/IEC 27001 wants detailed guidance on implementing individual information security controls. Which companion standard provides this?
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27002 provides a reference set of information security controls with implementation guidance. ISO 22301 covers business continuity, and 27701 covers privacy information management.

questions.prompt: Which NIST publication provides a comprehensive catalog of security and privacy controls for information systems and organizations?
questions.explanation: SP 800-53 is the control catalog. SP 800-88 covers media sanitization, 800-61 incident handling and 800-63 digital identity.

questions.prompt: Sales staff carry laptops containing customer data while traveling. Which control BEST protects the confidentiality of that data if a laptop is stolen?
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption keeps data unreadable without the key, protecting confidentiality. Backups protect availability rather than confidentiality.

questions.prompt: A system has a known vulnerability, but it is isolated and no threat exists that could ever reach or exploit it. How should the risk be described?
choices: Very low, since no threat can exploit the flaw
Impossible to rate without a full penetration test
Critical, since every vulnerability is high risk
Equal to the full replacement value of the system
questions.explanation: Risk exists when a threat can exploit a vulnerability to harm an asset. Without a credible threat, the risk is minimal, though conditions should still be monitored.

questions.prompt: What is the MAIN difference between violating an internal policy and violating a regulation such as HIPAA?
choices: There is no meaningful difference between them
A regulation violation can bring legal penalties
Regulations apply only to government agencies
Policies are mandatory, but regulations are only advice
questions.explanation: Regulations are laws enforced by government bodies, so violations can bring fines or other legal penalties. Policy violations are handled internally, usually through discipline.

questions.prompt: A research department cannot meet the company's password policy because a legacy instrument only supports short passwords. What is the BEST way to handle this?
choices: Rewrite the entire password policy to suit the instrument
Ignore the policy there without telling anyone
Disconnect the department from all networks permanently
questions.explanation: Policy exceptions should be formally requested, risk-assessed, approved by management and documented, usually with compensating controls.

questions.prompt: Many U.S. states have laws requiring organizations to notify affected residents when their personal information is exposed in a security incident. What are these laws called?
questions.explanation: Breach notification laws require timely notice to individuals, and sometimes regulators, after personal information is compromised.

questions.prompt: A company gives an outside IT support vendor remote access to its internal network. Which risk does this MOST directly introduce?
choices: Residual risk that has been reduced to zero
Third-party risk from the vendor's own weaknesses
Inherent risk that can never be managed
Lower risk, since the vendor assumes all accountability
questions.explanation: Granting vendors access creates third-party risk: a breach at the vendor can become a path into the company. Vendor assessments and least privilege help manage it.

questions.prompt: A competitor hires someone to secretly obtain a company's product designs and pricing plans. Which type of threat does this represent?
questions.explanation: Stealing trade secrets for a business advantage is corporate (industrial) espionage. Hacktivists are motivated by social or political causes.

questions.prompt: Which sequence BEST describes the general flow of the risk management process?
choices: Treat risks, identify them, monitor them, then assess them
Identify risks, assess them, treat them, then monitor them
Assess controls, buy insurance, then identify assets
Monitor risks, accept them, then identify them
questions.explanation: Risks are first identified, then assessed for likelihood and impact, then treated, and finally monitored over time as conditions change.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes the difference between confidentiality and privacy?
choices: Confidentiality covers only personal data, while privacy covers every kind of data
Privacy is a technical control, while confidentiality is a law
They are two names for the same property
Confidentiality limits disclosure; privacy is a person's rights over their data
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is about keeping any sensitive information from unauthorized parties. Privacy is about individuals' rights to control how their personal information is collected and used.

questions.prompt: A company outsources its payroll processing to a cloud provider to reduce risk. If the provider suffers a breach of employee data, who remains accountable to the employees and regulators?
choices: No one, because the risk was transferred
The company that outsourced the processing
Only the cloud provider that was breached
questions.explanation: Outsourcing can transfer some risk and operational responsibility, but the organization remains accountable for protecting the data it collects.

questions.prompt: A security team studies information about active attacker groups, the tools and techniques they use, and their indicators of compromise to anticipate attacks. What is this information called?
questions.explanation: Threat intelligence is evidence-based knowledge about threats and threat actors that helps organizations prepare defenses.

questions.prompt: Which administrative control helps reduce insider threat risk BEFORE a person joins the organization?
questions.explanation: Background checks screen candidates before they are given access. The other controls apply after an employee has joined or is leaving.

questions.prompt: A customer asks a company covered by the GDPR to provide a copy of all the personal data it holds about them. Which data subject right is the customer exercising?
questions.explanation: The right of access lets individuals obtain confirmation and a copy of the personal data an organization processes about them. Erasure is a request to delete it.

questions.prompt: A country's law requires that its citizens' personal data be stored and processed only within its borders. What is this requirement called?
questions.explanation: Data sovereignty (often called data residency) requires data to stay within a specific jurisdiction and be subject to its laws. Data remanence refers to leftover data on media.

questions.prompt: A system administrator compares current configuration file hashes with stored known-good hashes to detect any unauthorized modifications. Which security property is being protected?
questions.explanation: Comparing hashes detects changes, which protects integrity. Confidentiality concerns unauthorized disclosure rather than modification.

questions.prompt: A fire breaks out in a company's main office during business hours. According to business continuity and disaster recovery principles, what is the HIGHEST priority?
questions.explanation: Human life and safety always come first in any disaster or emergency. Systems and data are recovered afterwards.

questions.prompt: An organization contracts for a self-contained trailer equipped with computers, power and communications that can be driven to any location after a disaster. What type of recovery site is this?
questions.explanation: A mobile site is a portable, self-contained recovery facility that can be moved where needed. Hot and cold sites are fixed locations.

questions.prompt: A server stores identical copies of its data on two disks so it keeps running if one disk fails. Which RAID level does this describe?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two disks, so either disk can fail without data loss. RAID 0 offers no redundancy.

questions.prompt: Which backup type takes the LEAST time to run each night because it copies only data changed since the most recent backup of any kind?
questions.explanation: Incremental backups copy only changes since the last backup, so they are quickest to create, though restoring requires the full backup plus every incremental.

questions.prompt: A ransomware outbreak hits a company's file servers. Instead of improvising, responders follow a predefined, step-by-step guide written for ransomware incidents. What is this guide called?
questions.explanation: A playbook gives specific, repeatable response steps for a particular type of incident. A risk register tracks risks rather than response actions.

questions.prompt: During business continuity planning, a team discovers that all customer orders pass through a single internet connection with no backup. What does this connection represent?
questions.explanation: A single point of failure is one component whose failure stops the whole process. Adding a redundant connection removes it.

questions.prompt: A business continuity plan names who will take charge if the CEO and other senior leaders are unavailable during a disaster. What is this element of the plan called?
questions.explanation: An order of succession defines who assumes leadership authority if key leaders are unavailable. A call tree defines how staff are notified.

questions.prompt: During an incident, responders suspect the attacker has access to the company's email system. How should the response team communicate?
choices: Use an out-of-band channel such as phones
Post status updates on the public website
Keep using company email but mark it urgent
Wait until the incident ends to communicate
questions.explanation: If attackers may be monitoring normal channels, responders should use out-of-band communication so the attacker cannot see the response plans.

questions.prompt: Under the GDPR, when a data controller discovers a personal data breach that poses a risk to individuals, how soon must it normally notify the supervisory authority?
choices: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of it
Only if the news media reports it
Within 30 days of the breach occurring
Within one year of the breach
questions.explanation: GDPR requires notification to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach.

questions.prompt: After a regional disaster, the recovery team must decide which systems to restore first at the alternate site. What should guide this order?
choices: Whichever systems are quickest to restore
The order in which systems were purchased
The criticality and RTOs from the BIA
The departments that complain the loudest
questions.explanation: The BIA identifies the most critical functions and their recovery time objectives, so systems with the shortest RTOs and highest criticality are restored first.

questions.prompt: Before issuing a new contractor an account and badge, the security office checks the person's government-issued photo ID and confirms their identity with the hiring manager. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Identity proofing verifies that people are who they claim to be before credentials are issued. Authorization happens later, when granting permissions.

questions.prompt: A badge system rejects a card that is used to enter a secure area a second time without first being used to exit. Which feature prevents one badge from being passed back to let another person in?
questions.explanation: Anti-passback requires an exit record before the same badge can enter again, stopping users from passing a badge to someone else.

questions.prompt: An organization wants to be able to prove exactly which commands each administrator ran on critical servers. Which control BEST provides this accountability?
choices: Allowing administrators to edit their own audit logs
Disabling audit logging to improve server performance
Giving all administrators one shared admin account
Recording privileged sessions under individual accounts
questions.explanation: Recording privileged sessions under unique accounts ties each action to a specific person. Shared accounts and editable logs destroy accountability.

questions.prompt: A new Windows server includes a built-in guest account that no one needs. What should the administrator do with it?
choices: Add it to the administrators group
Give it a simple, well-known password
questions.explanation: Unneeded default accounts, such as guest, should be disabled to reduce the attack surface. Enabling or privileging them creates easy entry points.

questions.prompt: A company removes local administrator rights from all standard user workstations. Which risk does this MOST directly reduce?
choices: Malware installing itself with full system rights
Power failures affecting the whole office
questions.explanation: Without admin rights, users and any malware they run cannot make system-wide changes or install most software. This applies least privilege to endpoints.

questions.prompt: Two analysts both hold Secret clearances, but only one is assigned to Project Falcon. The other is denied access to Falcon's Secret files. Which principle explains the denial?
questions.explanation: A clearance alone is not enough; access also requires a legitimate need to know the specific information for assigned work.

questions.prompt: When an employee leaves, why do many organizations disable the account first instead of deleting it immediately?
choices: So the former employee can log in if needed
Because deleted accounts can never be recreated
To keep its data and audit history available
Because disabling is required to reset passwords
questions.explanation: Disabling stops all access while keeping files, ownership and logs available for investigations or handover. The account can be deleted later per policy.

questions.prompt: An employee often works on confidential financial reports while sitting on trains. Which physical control BEST reduces the risk of shoulder surfing?
choices: A host-based firewall on the laptop
A privacy screen filter on the display
A cable lock attached to the laptop
questions.explanation: A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle so nearby people cannot read the screen. Encryption protects stored data, not what is visible on screen.

questions.prompt: An administrator increases the sensitivity of a fingerprint reader protecting a server room. What is the MOST likely result?
choices: Both error rates drop to zero
More false acceptances and fewer false rejections
Fewer false acceptances but more false rejections
The crossover error rate no longer applies
questions.explanation: Making a biometric system stricter lowers the false acceptance rate but causes more legitimate users to be rejected, raising the false rejection rate.

questions.prompt: Why do many organizations print the holder's photograph on employee ID badges?
choices: To make the badges cheaper to produce in bulk
So that badges never need to be revoked
So the badge can open doors without a reader
So staff can confirm the wearer is the badge's owner
questions.explanation: A photo lets people verify that the badge holder is its rightful owner, which helps detect lost or borrowed badges.

questions.prompt: A company manages all user accounts and permissions for every application from a single directory service administered by one security team. Which type of access control administration is this?
questions.explanation: Centralized administration manages access from one place, giving consistency and easier auditing. In decentralized administration, individual departments manage their own access.
