questions.prompt: An auditor needs to view the finance department's records but must not be able to change or delete them. Which permission should be granted?
questions.explanation: Read-only access lets the auditor view files without altering them, applying least privilege. Modify or full control would allow changes.

questions.prompt: An attacker uses a hidden reader to copy the data from employees' simple proximity badges and creates working duplicates. Which upgrade BEST counters this?
choices: Larger photos printed on each badge
Badges printed in color for each department
questions.explanation: Smart cards with cryptographic challenge-response cannot easily be cloned by reading their data. Simple proximity cards transmit a static ID that can be copied.

questions.prompt: Developers need to troubleshoot production issues by viewing application logs, but they should not change production systems. Which approach BEST applies least privilege?
choices: Grant read-only access to the production logs only
Share the production admin password with the team
Give developers full administrator rights in production
Let developers copy the entire production database to laptops
questions.explanation: Granting only read access to the specific logs needed meets the business need without allowing production changes.

questions.prompt: A user's phone receives dozens of MFA push approval requests late at night that they did not initiate, and they finally tap Approve to make them stop. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: MFA fatigue floods a user with push prompts, hoping they will approve one. Number matching and alerting users to deny unexpected prompts help prevent it.

questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of electronic badge locks over traditional mechanical keys for office doors?
choices: Access can be revoked instantly and entries logged
They physically cannot be shared between people
They need no ongoing administration at all
They keep working through any power outage
questions.explanation: Electronic systems let administrators revoke a lost badge instantly and keep an audit trail. A lost mechanical key typically requires rekeying the locks.

questions.prompt: In a mandatory access control system, who is allowed to change the security label on a classified document?
choices: The document's current reader, at their discretion
Any user who has been granted read access
Any user who creates the document
Only security administrators, per system policy
questions.explanation: In MAC, labels are controlled centrally by the system and its administrators. Owners cannot change them at their discretion, unlike in DAC.

questions.prompt: An employee reports that their hardware authentication token was lost on the way home. What should the security team do FIRST?
choices: Issue the same token serial number again
Wait a week to see if it is found
Revoke or disable the lost token
questions.explanation: A lost authenticator should be revoked immediately so anyone who finds it cannot use it. A replacement can then be issued.

questions.prompt: A user types their username into a login screen but has not yet entered a password. Which access control step has occurred?
questions.explanation: Entering a username is claiming an identity, which is identification. Authentication occurs when the user proves that identity, such as with a password.

questions.prompt: A company configures its web server software to run under a dedicated low-privilege service account rather than as root or administrator. What is the MAIN benefit?
choices: The server no longer needs regular patching
The web pages will load noticeably faster for users
Users of the website no longer need passwords
A compromise of the server yields only limited rights
questions.explanation: Running services with least privilege limits the damage an attacker can do through a compromised service. Patching is still required.

questions.prompt: A banking app lets users view balances after logging in, but asks them to authenticate again with a fingerprint before sending a large transfer. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Step-up authentication requires stronger or additional verification for higher-risk actions within a session.

questions.prompt: A biometric system lets an unauthorized person into a restricted area. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: A Type II error is a false acceptance, where an impostor is wrongly accepted. A Type I error is a false rejection of a legitimate user.

questions.prompt: An email client is configured to download messages using POP3 without encryption. Which default port does it use?
questions.explanation: POP3 uses TCP 110 by default. IMAP uses 143, SMTP uses 25, and POP3 over TLS uses 995.

questions.prompt: A firewall must allow unencrypted directory queries from applications to a directory server using LDAP. Which default port should be opened?
questions.explanation: LDAP uses port 389 by default. LDAPS uses 636, Kerberos uses 88 and SMB uses 445.

questions.prompt: Domain-joined computers request authentication tickets from a key distribution center. Which default port does Kerberos use?
questions.explanation: Kerberos uses port 88. LDAP is 389, NTP is 123 and RDP is 3389.

questions.prompt: Port numbers from 0 through 1023, used by common services such as HTTP and SSH, are known as:
questions.explanation: Ports 0 to 1023 are well-known ports assigned to common services. Registered ports run from 1024 to 49151, and dynamic or ephemeral ports from 49152 to 65535.

questions.prompt: An attacker floods a switch with frames from thousands of fake source MAC addresses until its address table fills and it starts sending traffic out every port. What is this attack?
questions.explanation: MAC flooding overflows the switch's address table so it behaves like a hub, letting the attacker sniff traffic. ARP poisoning maps an IP address to the attacker's MAC.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends ICMP echo requests to a network's broadcast address using the victim's IP address as the source, so every host replies to the victim. What is this attack?
questions.explanation: A smurf attack is an ICMP amplification attack that abuses broadcast addresses to flood the spoofed victim with replies.

questions.prompt: An IDS generates an alert for a normal file transfer between two internal servers that is not an attack. What is this outcome called?
questions.explanation: A false positive is an alert on benign activity. A false negative is a real attack that goes undetected.

questions.prompt: A security team wants an automated tool that probes hosts across the network and reports missing patches, open ports and insecure configurations. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: A vulnerability scanner checks systems against known weaknesses and reports findings. A packet sniffer only captures traffic.

questions.prompt: A company is moving to a public cloud where its virtual machines run on the same physical hardware as other customers' workloads. Which risk is MOST associated with this?
choices: Unlimited physical access for the company's staff
The provider no longer being responsible for security
Having to maintain the provider's data center
questions.explanation: Public clouds are multi-tenant, so strong isolation between customers is essential. The provider still secures the physical infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A sprinkler system in an unheated storage building keeps its pipes filled with pressurized air, and water flows in only after a sprinkler head opens, so the pipes do not freeze. Which type of system is this?
questions.explanation: Dry pipe systems hold air until activated, which suits cold areas. Wet pipe systems keep water in the pipes at all times.

questions.prompt: A data center wants a water-based fire suppression system that requires a separate detection event before water fills the pipes, reducing the chance of accidental discharge onto equipment. Which system is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Pre-action systems need a detection trigger to fill the pipes and then a heat-activated head to release water, making accidental discharge less likely.

questions.prompt: A data center experiences a prolonged period of lower-than-normal voltage from the utility. What is this condition called?
questions.explanation: A brownout is an extended period of low voltage. A blackout is a complete loss of power, while spikes and surges are increases in voltage.

questions.prompt: A host has an IPv6 address beginning with fe80::. What type of address is this?
questions.explanation: Addresses in fe80::/10 are link-local and are used only on the local network segment. The IPv6 loopback address is ::1.

questions.prompt: Users on a network suddenly receive IP addresses with an unknown default gateway. Investigation finds a device on the LAN answering DHCP requests that IT did not install. What is this?
questions.explanation: A rogue DHCP server can hand out a malicious gateway or DNS server to redirect traffic. DHCP snooping on switches helps prevent it.

questions.prompt: A home office router has Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) PIN mode enabled. Why should it be disabled?
choices: It prevents WPA3 from encrypting wireless traffic
It turns off the router's built-in firewall
It hides the network's SSID from every user
Its PIN can be brute-forced to reveal the passphrase
questions.explanation: WPS PIN mode has a design flaw that lets attackers brute-force the PIN quickly and obtain the network passphrase.

questions.prompt: A user downloads a free utility that works as advertised but also gives an attacker hidden remote control of the computer. What type of malware is this?
questions.explanation: A remote access Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software while providing the attacker covert remote control. A worm spreads by itself.

questions.prompt: An attack runs malicious PowerShell commands directly in memory without writing any malware files to disk, making traditional file scanning ineffective. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Fileless malware uses legitimate built-in tools and runs in memory, leaving few files for antivirus to scan. Behavior-based detection is more effective.

questions.prompt: A company places a server in front of its internal web servers that receives all requests from the internet, forwards them inward and hides the internal servers' addresses. What is this server?
questions.explanation: A reverse proxy accepts inbound client requests on behalf of internal servers. A forward proxy makes outbound requests on behalf of internal users.

questions.prompt: An online store spreads incoming web requests across several identical web servers so no single server is overwhelmed and the site stays available if one fails. Which device does this?
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes traffic across multiple servers, improving performance and availability.

questions.prompt: Employees working from home need encrypted access from their laptops to internal company resources over the internet. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
choices: A VLAN on the office switch
questions.explanation: A remote-access VPN connects individual users securely to the corporate network. A site-to-site VPN links entire networks, such as two offices.

questions.prompt: A company offers Wi-Fi to visitors in its lobby. Which configuration BEST protects the internal network?
choices: Connect the guest AP directly to the internal LAN
Disable encryption on the corporate Wi-Fi network
Put guests on a separate, internet-only VLAN
Give guests the corporate Wi-Fi password
questions.explanation: Isolating guest traffic on its own segment with internet-only access keeps visitors' devices away from internal systems.

questions.prompt: An attacker sends ICMP echo requests to every address in a subnet to find out which hosts are online before attacking them. What is this reconnaissance technique?
questions.explanation: A ping sweep identifies live hosts by pinging a range of addresses. It is often a precursor to port scanning and attack.

questions.prompt: A company still manages network devices using SNMPv1. Why should it upgrade to SNMPv3?
choices: SNMPv3 runs only over TCP port 22 with SSH
SNMPv3 removes the need for monitoring
questions.explanation: SNMPv1 and v2c send community strings in clear text. SNMPv3 adds user authentication and encryption of messages.

questions.prompt: The Mirai botnet compromised hundreds of thousands of IoT cameras and routers. Which weakness did it MAINLY exploit?
choices: Zero-day flaws in the TLS 1.3 protocol
questions.explanation: Mirai scanned the internet for IoT devices that still used factory default credentials and logged in to them. Changing default passwords is a basic defense.

questions.prompt: A developer of a battery-powered mobile app wants asymmetric encryption that provides strong security with much smaller keys than RSA. Which option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: ECC offers security comparable to RSA with much shorter keys, saving processing power and battery. DES and 3DES are symmetric ciphers, and MD5 is a hash.

questions.prompt: Which set of details should each security log entry include so events can be investigated later?
choices: The user's password so the session can be replayed
Who did it, what happened, when and from where
Only the date on which the event took place
Only the name of the server that made the entry
questions.explanation: Useful log entries record the identity, the event, an accurate timestamp and the source. Passwords should never be written to logs.

questions.prompt: An IT team builds one fully patched, hardened operating system image and uses it to deploy every new workstation. What is this pre-configured image commonly called?
questions.explanation: A golden image is an approved, hardened template that ensures new systems start from a consistent secure baseline.

questions.prompt: An employee posts photos from inside the office on a public social network, revealing a whiteboard with network diagrams. Which policy MOST directly addresses this behavior?
questions.explanation: A social media policy defines what employees may share about the organization online, including restrictions on posting sensitive information.

questions.prompt: A company displays security posters in break rooms and sends short monthly reminder emails about locking screens. Which type of security education activity is this?
questions.explanation: Awareness activities keep security in people's attention with posters, reminders and briefings. Training builds specific job skills.

questions.prompt: A company's developers attend a multi-day hands-on course to learn secure coding techniques specific to their jobs. Which type of security activity is this?
questions.explanation: Training teaches the specific skills a role needs, such as secure coding. Awareness is broad attention-raising for everyone, and education builds deeper understanding.

questions.prompt: Attackers compromise a popular industry forum that a target company's engineers visit regularly, so that visitors' computers become infected. What is this attack called?
questions.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a site the targets are known to visit. Whaling targets senior executives directly with phishing.

questions.prompt: An attacker searches through a company's trash bins and finds printed employee lists and old invoices to use in a social engineering attack. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Dumpster diving is searching discarded material for useful information. Shredding sensitive documents is the main countermeasure.

questions.prompt: An administrator discovers that the private key for the company's web server certificate was accidentally published online. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Revoke the certificate and replace the key pair
Publish the matching public key online as well
Move the website to a different domain name
Keep using the certificate until it expires
questions.explanation: A compromised private key means anyone can impersonate the server, so the certificate must be revoked through the CA and replaced with a new key pair.

questions.prompt: An attacker hides stolen data inside ordinary-looking image files before sending them out of the network, so the data is concealed rather than encrypted. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Steganography conceals data inside other files, such as images or audio, so its existence is hidden. Encryption makes data unreadable but does not hide that it exists.

questions.prompt: What is the length of the hash value produced by SHA-256, regardless of the size of the input?
choices: It varies with the input size
questions.explanation: SHA-256 always produces a fixed-length 256-bit digest. Fixed-length output is a property of all hash functions.

questions.prompt: Security analysts receive thousands of SIEM alerts each day, most of them harmless, and are starting to ignore them. What is the BEST action?
choices: Hire more staff to click through every alert without changes
Tune the alert rules to reduce false positives
questions.explanation: Tuning rules to filter known benign activity reduces alert fatigue so analysts can focus on real threats.

questions.prompt: An email claims to come from the company's IT department, but the sender's address uses the domain examp1e-support.com instead of example.com. What should employees learn to recognize here?
choices: A legitimate internal email alias for IT
A sign that the email has been encrypted
A lookalike domain, a common phishing sign
A normal message from an external IT vendor
questions.explanation: Phishing emails often use domains that look similar to real ones. Awareness training teaches staff to check the full sender address before acting.

questions.prompt: An employee loses a personal smartphone that is enrolled in the company's mobile device management system and contains corporate email. What should IT do?
choices: Wait a few weeks to see if the phone is found
Change the company's wireless network name
Remotely lock it and wipe corporate data
Disable the employee's building access badge
questions.explanation: MDM lets IT remotely lock a lost device and wipe corporate data so it cannot be accessed by whoever finds it.

questions.prompt: A vulnerability scan finds a critical flaw on an internet-facing web server and a low-severity flaw on an isolated internal printer. Which should be patched first and why?
choices: The printer, because it is easier to patch
The web server: critical and internet-exposed
Neither, until the next annual review cycle
Either one, because the order does not matter
questions.explanation: Patches should be prioritized by severity and exposure. An internet-facing system with a critical flaw is the most likely to be attacked.

questions.prompt: Why do security policies require encryption keys to be replaced on a regular schedule?
choices: Because keys lose strength each time they are used
To make the encryption algorithm run faster
So that users can choose their own new keys
To limit data exposed if a key is compromised
questions.explanation: Key rotation limits the amount of data protected by any one key and the time an attacker could use a stolen key.

questions.prompt: An organization stores copies of its encryption keys with a trusted third party so they can be recovered if needed, for example under a legal order. What is this practice called?
questions.explanation: Key escrow places copies of keys with a trusted party for recovery. Key stretching strengthens weak passwords against brute force.

questions.prompt: A tool learns each user's normal login times, locations and file access, then alerts when an account suddenly downloads large amounts of data at 3 a.m. What is this tool?
questions.explanation: UEBA (user and entity behavior analytics) builds behavioral baselines and flags deviations that may indicate compromised accounts or insider threats.
